facts.text: By late September the maintained White River trail beyond the Boulder Creek turnoff had been brushed, and the abandoned track toward Thunder Creek was mostly followable.
Above a camp at about 4,200 ft by Thunder Creek, dense slide alder between roughly 4,200 and 5,000 ft is the hardest bushwhacking before Thunder Basin opens up.
By late September the south-east gully below the notch is bare and loose, and large rocks release easily.

notes: Only the White River approach was a day trip in the harvest. No track qualifies.
